subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw core add a separate LLM contextual activation state machine for group chats, or should maintainers steer this toward existing ambient room-event behavior and narrower plugin/API work?
rationale: The source shows the requested behavior is not implemented, but adding it changes group privacy, provider exposure, config shape, logs, CLI surface, and Telegram/WhatsApp delivery semantics; automation cannot choose that product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Use ambient/plugin path first
options.body: Keep the issue open for design, document the current ambient room-event path as the supported workaround, and only add a narrow plugin/API seam if existing surfaces cannot host the feature.

options.title: Sponsor core contextual activation
options.body: Accept the broader core feature direction and require a design with provider/privacy policy, config migration/doctor handling, multi-channel proof, and security review before implementation.

options.title: Close as out of core scope
options.body: Decline the core state machine and close this umbrella in favor of ClawHub/plugin work plus narrower issues for missing extension APIs.

recommendation.title: Use ambient/plugin path first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for design, document the current ambient room-event path as the supported workaround, and only add a narrow plugin/API seam if existing surfaces cannot host the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current-main history ties steipete to ambient room-event docs/core classifier work and VISION.md product-boundary guidance.
